taurajo_word_from_bael_modan.description:
Wrangler Tull. Come round the fire, you're in the smoke.

The dwarves have been digging at Bael Modan for years and nobody here has minded very much.

I want to be fair about that. Digging is digging. They turned up, they put a hole in some ground nobody was grazing, and for a long while that was the whole story and the camp had bigger ones.

Word now is they've built a proper fortress over it. Bael'dun Keep.

That's a different sentence.

You don't build a keep over a hole unless you intend to be at the bottom of that hole for a very long time, or unless you expect somebody to come and stop you.

Either way it stops being mining.

Go and see for yourself before Camp Taurajo commits any real attention south.

I'd rather look foolish for asking than find out from a dwarf.
taurajo_word_from_bael_modan.accept_text: Bael Modan, south - look for the keep over the dig.
taurajo_word_from_bael_modan.turn_in_text:
A whole keep. Just for digging up old bones and ore.

Dwarves.

Still - good to know what we're dealing with, and better to know it now.

taurajo_dwarven_excavation.description:
Keep's confirmed, so now the dig itself.

And I'd like to put a number on the thing that's actually bothering me, because it isn't the hole.

That excavation has expanded further into tauren-claimed ground every season I've watched it. Not once. Every season.

A little each time. Never enough to be worth a complaint, and that's precisely the method - whether or not anyone down there is thinking of it as one.

I drove kodo past that boundary stone for twenty years. It is now a long way inside their workings and nobody ever crossed a line, because the line moved under it a yard at a time.

So I want the crews thinned.

Miners, engineers, it doesn't matter to me.

Just fewer dwarves expanding that dig, and a season where the stone stays where it is.
taurajo_dwarven_excavation.accept_text: The excavation crews at the Bael Modan dig.
taurajo_dwarven_excavation.turn_in_text:
That'll slow their digging a season at least.

I'll go and look at the boundary stone this week. First time in three years I'll be able to stand at it.

Thank you.

taurajo_general_twinbraids_folly.description:
[Elder Longtread takes his time with this one.]

I have watched General Twinbraid grow bolder with every site he claims.

And I want to be exact about why I'm asking, because this will look like vengeance and it is not.

I have no quarrel with dwarves. I've traded with them. I knew one well, some years back, and I'd have called him a friend if either of us had used the word.

Twinbraid doesn't dig for ore anymore. Not really.

He digs for territory and calls it prospecting, and the calling-it is the part that matters, because a man who's found a word for what he's doing has stopped hearing anyone tell him not to.

He has stopped respecting any boundary at all. Not ours. Not his own Keep's.

Someone needs to remind him where Bael'dun's walls actually end.

I'd have preferred that to be a conversation. It was, twice.
taurajo_general_twinbraids_folly.accept_text: At Bael'dun Keep, with the dig crews he commands.
taurajo_general_twinbraids_folly.turn_in_text:
Twinbraid's dead, and the digging stops for a while.

It'll start again eventually. It always does - somebody else will have the same idea and a better word for it.

But this bought the land some peace, and peace is bought, never given.

ratchet_raptor_hides.description:
Fishmonger Gribble. Yes, I know what the stall says. Hear me out.

I've got a side trade in raptor hide.

Fish is the business. Fish is reliable, fish is boring, and fish has kept this stall open through two bad years.

Raptor hide is the margin.

And the Sunscale out at the Grounds east of here are the closest real supply on this whole coast - everything else comes up from the south at a price that eats the point of it.

Bring them back whole, as whole as you can manage.

That's not fussiness. A hide with a hole through the middle is worth about a third, because the buyers cut panels and a panel has to be clean. I've watched a man price a perfectly good hide down to nothing over one spear mark.

Whole as you can. I'll make it worth your trip.
ratchet_raptor_hides.accept_text: Sunscale raptors at the Grounds, east of Ratchet.
ratchet_raptor_hides.turn_in_text:
Good hide. Barely torn.

This'll fetch a real price at the docks, and I'll not be telling anyone where it came from.

ratchet_thinning_the_grounds.description:
Dockmaster Brindle. Walk and talk, I've got a tide.

I have had one too many shipments delayed by raptors.

Not attacked. Delayed - and I want the distinction on the record because every time I raise this, somebody asks how many drivers I've lost and the answer is none.

Here's what actually happens. The Sunscale stray too close to the coast road. The drivers see them. The drivers stop, or turn back, or take the long way round, and a shipment that should take two days takes four.

Nobody dies. Everybody's late. And late, in this port, is a contract.

I've lost two this quarter to a problem that has never once drawn blood.

So: thin them back from the Grounds itself.

Not the road - the road's a symptom. They're coming off the Grounds because there's too many on it.

My shipments cannot keep dodging claws.
ratchet_thinning_the_grounds.accept_text: At the Raptor Grounds, back from the coast road.
ratchet_thinning_the_grounds.turn_in_text:
Fewer raptors between here and the Grounds.

The road's clear. For now, which is the only tense this port deals in.

ratchet_brontus.description:
Now this one's half business and I'll tell you which half.

Brontus.

Every sailor who's been inland has a story about that kodo, and I've been collecting them for six years without ever intending to.

Ancient. Elite - and I use that word deliberately, because the stories agree on it and sailors agree on nothing. A beast old enough to have a reputation that arrived in this port before I did.

Half of those stories are probably true. That's my honest estimate and it's a generous one.

The trouble is which half, because the dangerous half is real whichever way round it goes. He roams Blackthorn Ridge and my drivers go round it, and going round costs me.

So: hunt him.

Bring back proof and I'll believe the rest of it.

And then I'll tell the story myself, badly, for years. I want you to know that going in.
ratchet_brontus.turn_in_text:
You actually did it.

I'll be telling this story myself now, and I'll be getting it wrong within a fortnight.

Well earned.

ratchet_zulrakas_toll.description:
Zulraka. Dockhand - which means I walk, mon, more than anybody here realises.

There's a silithid dig south-east of this port, spiralling down into the earth, and I've heard it's been growing.

Now I know how that sounds coming from a dockhand. I'm not a scholar and I've got no business having a theory about bugs.

Here's my business.

I walk the coast road every week. Same road, same stretch, since I came to this port - and the thing about walking a road for years is you learn what it sounds like under your feet.

It's different past the fourth mile. Hollower. Has been since spring.

If that dig keeps going it undermines the road, and then one week it isn't a road and I'm on it.

Go look. Tell me how deep it goes.

I'd rather know than keep guessing at it every Thursday.
ratchet_zulrakas_toll.accept_text: The silithid dig south-east of Ratchet.
ratchet_zulrakas_toll.turn_in_text:
Deeper than I hoped. Not as deep as I feared.

Thank you for checking, mon. I'll sleep easier walking that road - and I'll still walk the inland side of it.

org_quilboar_territories.description:
Krunk Anvilfist. Mind the anvil, it's hot and it's been hot since Tuesday.

Blackthorn Ridge, north of Razorfen Kraul.

Razormane country. And the reports say it's thick with them now - properly held, not just wandered through.

I'd like that confirmed before I waste a warband on a rumour, and I've wasted one before and I've not been allowed to forget it.

Here's what I need and it isn't a headcount.

I need to know whether that ridge is a camp or a position. A camp is quilboar living somewhere. A position is quilboar holding something, and the two look identical from a distance and are completely different problems.

So go up and survey it.

And if there's a name up there - somebody they follow - I want that most of all. Numbers I can plan around. A name changes what I send.
org_quilboar_territories.accept_text: Blackthorn Ridge, north of Razorfen Kraul.
org_quilboar_territories.turn_in_text:
Confirmed, then. Thick with quilboar, and at least one real threat worth naming.

I'll pass this up the chain. And this time they'll read it, because it's got a name in it.

org_razormane_incursion.description:
Ridge confirmed, so we bleed it.

And I'll be straight about the goal, which is not conquest and never was.

I want the Razormane to reconsider testing us.

That's it. I'm not taking that ridge - I haven't the men and I wouldn't hold it if I had. What I want is for the next quilboar who suggests pushing toward the southern trade routes to be argued with by somebody in his own camp.

That argument only happens if this raid costs them.

A small raid they shrug off. A real one gets talked about round their own fire, and the talking is the whole objective.

The stalkers work the ridge, so that's where you'll find them.

Whichever rank you come across. It's not about which ones - it's about how many, and how obviously.
org_razormane_incursion.accept_text: The Razormane stalkers on Blackthorn Ridge.
org_razormane_incursion.turn_in_text:
The ridge won't forget this raid.

And they'll think twice next time, which is a thing I can't make happen with a warband and you just did in an afternoon.

org_hagg_taurenbane.description:
There's a champion up on that ridge and I need him dead before he becomes a story.

Hagg Taurenbane.

He's earned the name the hard way - ask any patrol that's crossed him and lived, and there are fewer of those than I'd like to say out loud.

Here's the part that's actually urgent, and it isn't the killing.

Solo warbands have stopped patrolling that stretch. Entirely. Not after an order - they just stopped, one at a time, and nobody reported it and I only noticed from the duty rosters.

That's what a reputation does before the fighting even starts. He's taken a mile of ground off us without leaving his ridge.

Kill him before the Razormane rally round the idea of him.

Because once a tribe decides a man is unkillable, killing him stops being enough - you have to do it in front of them, and that's a much harder afternoon.
org_hagg_taurenbane.accept_text: On Blackthorn Ridge, among the Razormane.
org_hagg_taurenbane.turn_in_text:
He bled like anything else does.

The stories will outlive him anyway - they always do.

At least they're just stories now, and the patrols will go back out.

org_snizzles_curiosity.description:
Snizzle Boltcrank. Don't touch anything on that bench, most of it is mid-experiment and one of it is mid-argument.

There's a genuinely new silithid tunnel network south-east of Ratchet.

New. I want to dwell on that word because everybody skips past it.

Silithid nests are old. That's the whole character of the things - you find one, and it turns out it's been there since before anybody local had a word for it. I have never in my career heard of one appearing.

This one appeared.

So something changed, recently, in a species that does not change, and I would very much like to know what.

I want chitin. Hardened chitin - the kind that comes off something that has actually fought for its life, not the soft rubbish off surface vermin.

The hardening is the data. A creature that's had to armour itself was expecting something.
org_snizzles_curiosity.accept_text: Off the silithid in the new tunnels south-east of Ratchet.
org_snizzles_curiosity.turn_in_text:
Fascinating structure. Look at the layering - that's not growth, that's response.

This'll keep me occupied for weeks.

Thank you. Genuinely, and I don't say that at this bench.

org_into_the_broodspiral.description:
Apothecary Zurm. Come in, mind the step, ignore the smell - it's the work, not the room.

I have become concerned about what's at the centre of that tunnel network, and I'd like to explain the shape of the concern.

It isn't the silithid. Silithid are a known quantity and an unpleasant one and we have dealt with nests before.

It's the spiral.

A nest spreads. It goes where the digging is easy, it branches, it wanders - that's what every silithid warren I've studied does and it's what makes them survivable.

This one descends in a spiral, which is to say it is going somewhere specific, and something decided where.

So I want it confirmed properly rather than rumoured about by dockhands.

Clear the guardians off the outer tunnels.

And then we'll know whether this is worth Orgrimmar's real attention, which is a sentence I have been avoiding writing for a month.
org_into_the_broodspiral.accept_text: The outer tunnels of the Broodspiral, south-east of Ratchet.
org_into_the_broodspiral.turn_in_text:
Ten down, and the tunnels keep going deeper than that.

Whatever's at the centre of that spiral, it's not finished growing.

I've written that down and I dislike it in my own handwriting.

org_the_broodkeeper.description:
Outer tunnels are confirmed dangerous, which I'd expected, and confirmed organised, which I had not.

There's a Broodkeeper deeper in the spiral. A caster of sorts, tending the egg chambers.

Tending. That's the word I keep coming back to and it's the reason I'm sending you rather than writing another report.

Silithid don't tend. They lay and they leave and the hive works or it doesn't. Every text I own agrees on that and two of them are from people who died establishing it.

Something down there is looking after eggs deliberately, and the growth rate we've measured is exactly what you'd expect if it were.

Every day it lives, the hive gets bigger. Not linearly.

Kill it and buy the surface world some real time - which is all I'm claiming, because the eggs are already laid and nothing kills those but years.
org_the_broodkeeper.accept_text: The egg chambers deeper in the Broodspiral.
org_the_broodkeeper.turn_in_text:
The egg chambers have gone quiet. For now.

It won't stay that way forever. It'll stay that way long enough, which is the only promise anyone in my trade gets to make.

org_the_queens_silence.description:
I've confirmed what I feared and I'm going to say it plainly rather than hedge it in the way I've been hedging it for a fortnight.

Something massive rules the centre of that spiral.

A Queen. And everything down there answers to her, which is the part that turns a nest into a problem.

Here's the distinction and it's the whole of my argument.

An unorganised hive is a hazard. It eats what's near it, it grows where the ground allows, and you can live beside one for a generation if you're sensible about which fields you plant.

An organised one decides.

And I have watched this one dig a spiral toward something, tend its own eggs, and armour its workers against a threat it was anticipating - and I do not know what it's anticipating, and that is the single most uncomfortable sentence in my notes.

Kill her and the hive loses its reason to keep growing.

This is the real fight. Everything before it was the approach, including the parts that nearly killed you.
org_the_queens_silence.turn_in_text:
The Broodspiral is silent now.

It won't stay empty - nothing in the Barrens ever does, and I'd not insult you by pretending otherwise.

But for now it's quiet. You did something genuinely difficult down there. Don't let anyone tell you otherwise, and somebody will.

taurajo_beastcallers_request.description:
Beastcaller Nira. Quietly, there's one sleeping.

I want Sunscale eggs. From the Grounds east of here, off the lashtails that guard them.

Three, and unbroken if you can manage it, and I'll tell you exactly why that's worth more to me than a wagon of hides.

I think I can hatch one.

Not tame a caught raptor - that's been done and it's a miserable business for everyone involved, and the animal never stops knowing. Hatch one. Have it know me before it knows anything else.

I've been working toward it for six years and I've had two eggs in that time and lost both, one to a crack I didn't see and one to my own impatience.

So: carefully.

Unbroken means unbroken. A hairline is a dead raptor three weeks later and you won't know until it is.

A hatched raptor's worth more to me than a dozen hides. It's worth more to me than most things.
taurajo_beastcallers_request.accept_text: Sunscale eggs from the Grounds east of camp. Unbroken.
taurajo_beastcallers_request.turn_in_text:
Still warm!

This might actually work. I'm not going to say more than that - I've said more than that before.

Thank you. Truly, this is rare work.

taurajo_spiritcarvers_balance.description:
Sit with me. I've been needing somebody who's actually seen it rather than heard about it.

Spiritcarver Dennok.

Here's what I've been turning over, and I'd like to lay it out in order because the order is the thing that worries me.

Quilboar against quilboar, north. That's been true for generations and I'd have called it the natural state of the plain.

Dwarves digging where they shouldn't, south. Three years of that, maybe four, and getting faster.

And something ancient waking in the earth beneath both of them.

Any one of those is a season's problem. I've carved totems for worse.

All three at once, in one lifetime, on one plain - that's not three problems. That's one thing happening, and I cannot see the shape of it, and I have been staring at it long enough to know that staring is no longer helping.

So tell me what you saw. All of it, in your own order.

I need to think this through with somebody whose hands were in it.
taurajo_spiritcarvers_balance.accept_text: Sit with Spiritcarver Dennok a while.
taurajo_spiritcarvers_balance.turn_in_text:
You've given me a clearer picture than I had, and a worse one.

Whatever comes of it, at least I'm not guessing anymore.

Thank you. Come back if you see more - and you will.

sb_hawks_over_the_rift.description:
Brakka Stonehoof. Stand back from the edge while we talk - not for the drop, for the updraft.

The Rift is a day's walk of broken canyon between Camp Taurajo and everything south of it. There is no way round. People try, every season, and the Waystation goes out and finds what's left of them.

I keep the ramp that crosses it. That's the job and there's no other job here.

The cliffhawks have started nesting in the walls.

And here's the thing I want you to understand, because it changes how you fight them: they don't mind the caravans at all. A wagon could go past a nest all day.

They mind the people on the ramp, who they see - quite reasonably, from where they're sitting - as dinner.

Brown wings, white throats, and a great deal of attitude.

Thin them along the walls.

And don't fall in. The Rift is not forgiving about that and I have never once had to say it twice to the same person.
sb_hawks_over_the_rift.accept_text: Along the canyon walls either side of the ramp.
sb_hawks_over_the_rift.turn_in_text:
Quieter already. I can hear the wagons again.

Take this. It's the least the Waystation owes you.

sb_geodes_for_the_warden.description:
Now something my wardens worked out on their own, and I'm still proud of them for it.

The gravel skitterers down on the Rift floor carry geodes in their shells. Like pockets - they're not eating them, they're not using them, they just have them.

And the crystals inside hum before a rockfall.

Not during. Before. One of my people noticed her bag singing and stepped left, and the ramp she'd been standing on went into the canyon about four seconds later.

A string of them along that ramp is worth a warden's life. I can say that with a figure attached, which is not something I usually get to do.

They are, unhappily, worth a skitterer's life too, and I'd rather own that than let it go unsaid.

Glittering things inside the shell. You can't miss them.

And if the skitterer objects, don't take it personally.
sb_geodes_for_the_warden.accept_text: Off the gravel skitterers on the Rift floor.
sb_geodes_for_the_warden.turn_in_text:
They hum! Listen to that.

That's one fewer funeral this season, and I know exactly whose.

Take this.

sb_teeth_in_the_canyon.description:
The sabertooths came down out of the high rock three weeks ago.

That's not normal. They've got everything they need up there - I've watched that population for six years and they have never once had a reason to come to the ramp.

A caravan of kodo-haulers lost two animals and a driver.

And every survivor off that caravan told me the same thing, separately, without conferring: something bigger than a sabertooth was watching from the ledges.

They had a name for it. Dustmaw.

I've heard that name before. My mother used it to get me off the ramp at dusk, and I'd put it away with the rest of the stories about forty years ago.

The cats first. They're the sure thing and they're what's killing people.

Dustmaw, if he shows himself, is the reason the cats came down at all.

He's half the canyon's size and twice as stubborn.
sb_teeth_in_the_canyon.accept_text: On the ramp and the ledges above it.
sb_teeth_in_the_canyon.turn_in_text:
Dustmaw. Dead.

I'll hang a fang over the gate, and I'll take it down again the first time a child asks me whether the story's true.

You've earned a bigger share than that.

sb_across_the_rift.description:
Two other ramps cross this Rift besides mine, and I haven't had a warden near either since the cliffhawks started.

That's four months. I want to say that plainly because it's a failure and it's mine - I had the people and I kept them here, on the ramp I could see, which is exactly the decision that loses you the other two.

Walk the west ramp. Then the east.

And tell me what's on them.

The Rift is wider than it looks from up here and it is always quieter than it should be, and both of those things are how people get into trouble down there.

Look for hawks, cats, and anything that has no business on a ramp.

Bones are normal. We've been losing animals off these crossings since the Waystation went up.

Fresh bones are not. If you find fresh, come straight back and don't go further.
sb_across_the_rift.accept_text: West ramp first, then the east one.
sb_across_the_rift.turn_in_text:
Both passable. Good.

The Waystation can breathe, and I can finally put wardens back where they should have been.

Take this - and think of me kindly when you cross.

sb_hyenas_in_the_bones.description:
Rurk. Bone-hunter, and before you make the face - everybody makes the face - it's a trade and it feeds people.

Giant bones. The kind that stick up out of the Field of Giants like the ribs of a ship, and they've been there longer than anyone has a story for.

The hyenas have made it harder.

And they've made it harder in a clever way, which I resent more than the danger. They've learned that a man with his arms full of bones is a man who can't swing a spear.

So they wait. They let you load up. And then they come in a pack, and you've got a choice between your morning's work and your arm.

Spotted, patient, and cheerful about all of it.

Drive them off the bones.

I'll make a good deal more of a living if I'm not being chased across a plain I'm meant to be working.
sb_hyenas_in_the_bones.accept_text: Out among the bones on the Field of Giants.
sb_hyenas_in_the_bones.turn_in_text:
Mmm. Hear that? Nothing.

You'd be surprised how good that sounds after a season of it.

Take this.

sb_giants_knucklebones.description:
The old plain has more than bones in it. It's got something that wears them.

Bone-dust wraiths. Dust-grey, and they drift between the ribs out there carrying knuckles the size of anvils, up on the shoulder, like a man carrying a sack.

They keep them close. The way a miser keeps coins, and I've watched one put a knuckle down and pick it straight back up again.

I want those knuckles.

[He waits.]

I'm not going to tell you why, and I'd rather be short about it than lie to you, because I'll pay you enough that you don't need the reason.

Take what you can off them.

And don't let them take yours. That's not a joke I'm making. Watch the hands.
sb_giants_knucklebones.accept_text: Off the bone-dust wraiths among the ribs.
sb_giants_knucklebones.turn_in_text:
Look at the polish on that. Beautiful.

Take this - I'll be busy carving a while, and I'd rather be left to it.

sb_the_matriarchs_last_walk.description:
There's a herd-mother out on the Field of Giants walking in circles.

A season now. Same ground, same circle, goring anything that comes near her, and the herders call her Old Mother Longhorn.

She isn't mad. I need that said before I ask you.

She lost a calf. That's the whole of it - she lost it out there somewhere in the bones and she has been looking for it ever since, and the circle is the search.

The old and sorry ones of her herd are walking it with her. They'll come at you first.

[He doesn't look up.]

I won't do it myself. I'll tell you straight that I think it'd be bad luck on a man in my trade, and you can think what you like of that.

I pay well, though. And I'd ask you to be quick about it.

She's been grieving long enough.
sb_the_matriarchs_last_walk.accept_text: Out on the Field of Giants, where she walks her circle.
sb_the_matriarchs_last_walk.turn_in_text:
It's done, then.

Quietly, I hope.

Take this. And say a word for her at the gate, if you've got one in you.

sb_thrumbone.description:
There's something out there older than the bones.

I want you to sit with that sentence, because I've had three years with it. Those ribs have been on that plain since before anybody wrote anything down about this continent, and there is a thing walking among them that was there first.

The wraiths gather round it.

It walks a slow circle through the ribs, and when it does, the ground hums - and I've felt that hum in my feet from a mile off, through boots, standing still.

I call it Thrumbone. I named it myself, which I'm not proud of.

I've never seen it. I've had every chance and I've turned away from all of them and I don't intend to change that now.

I want it gone.

Wraiths first.

And then, if you feel the ground start to sing - that's him. I'd run. That's precisely why you're the one being paid.
sb_thrumbone.accept_text: Among the ribs on the Field of Giants. Wraiths first.
sb_thrumbone.turn_in_text:
The ground's gone quiet. First time in years.

I... thank you.

Take these. They belong to the plain now, and so do you, whether or not that's what you wanted.

sb_skinners_trophy_cords.description:
Oggra. I keep the thornwatch on the Razorfen approach and I've done it four winters, which is three more than anybody before me. Taurajo's called me in to report, and I'd like to go back out with some help.

The Razormane skinners have started wandering south of the Ridge.

They braid trophy cords out of whatever they kill. That's old practice, it's not new, and I'd not trouble you for a quilboar keeping to his own habits.

What's new is what's on them.

I want the cords.

Not for the trophies. For the names knotted into them - because a skinner knots who he took, and I have rangers who went south of that Ridge and did not come back, and I have never been able to write to a single one of their families with anything better than a guess.

Look for the small bell on the cord. That's how they recognise each other.

Bring them back and I'll read what they say.
sb_skinners_trophy_cords.accept_text: Off the Razormane skinners south of the Ridge. Look for the bell.
sb_skinners_trophy_cords.turn_in_text:
Names. Faces. A great many dead rangers.

I'll write to their families, properly, with something true in it.

Take this.

sb_the_boarhound_pack.description:
The Razormane keep boarhounds. Low, bristled, and built for charging through thorn - which is an awful thing to meet in thorn, because you can't.

That by itself is ordinary.

What isn't ordinary is how they're hunting now. Packs, along the ridge, pushing in one direction and holding a line while they do it.

There's a handler behind that. A quilboar, working those hounds, and he is a great deal better at it than I would like.

I've watched him turn a pack on a whistle. Not call them off - turn them, mid-charge, onto a flank.

I've got rangers who can't do that with rangers.

Hounds to the west of the ridge. Stalkers in the thorns behind them, which is the half people miss.

Both.

And if you find the handler out there, I'd very much like to hear about it before you do anything else.
sb_the_boarhound_pack.accept_text: Hounds west of the ridge, stalkers in the thorns behind.
sb_the_boarhound_pack.turn_in_text:
Better. The ridge sounds different.

I think I can hear the birds again, which I hadn't noticed stopping.

Take this.

sb_skinwalker_garn.description:
There's a story on Blackthorn Ridge, and I'd like to tell it to you the way I heard it rather than the way I believe it.

A Razormane called Garn. He skins what he kills and he wears what he takes.

I had that off three different people in four winters and I filed it with the rest of the thornwatch folklore - the singing well, the two-headed boar, the ranger who walks the ridge looking for his bow.

Then a ranger came back with half his coat missing.

Not torn. Missing - cut away clean, on a man who got out alive and could not afterwards tell me when it had happened.

So it's not folklore. It's a working method and I've been slow about it.

Garn works with seers. They're his eyes and they're how he gets close, so take them first - that's the whole of the plan and it's the right one.

Then him.

And watch his hands. He can wear a face the way you'd wear a hat.
sb_skinwalker_garn.accept_text: On the Ridge, with the Razormane seers. Seers first - they're his eyes.
sb_skinwalker_garn.turn_in_text:
Garn's dead. The Ridge feels lighter.

Take this - keep it close, and don't let anybody peel your coat.

sb_the_bramble_court.description:
South of my post the thorns grow thick and the quilboar grow thicker, and that's where this ends.

A Bristleback matriarch has taken the Razorfen approach for her court. Durga.

She's grown her bramble-guard around her like a hedge - and I use the word deliberately, because that's what it is. It isn't a bodyguard, it's a planted boundary with quilboar in it, and it's been getting wider all winter.

I've measured the hedge four times. It's a hundred paces further out than when I took the post.

Which means the Razorfen approach is closing, and when it closes, everything south of the Ridge belongs to her and we find out what she wants it for.

Guards, then the boars, then the queen. Don't change that order to be clever.

The thorns bite. The quilboar bite harder.

And stay on dry ground - that's not advice about footing.
sb_the_bramble_court.accept_text: South of the thornwatch, on the Razorfen approach.
sb_the_bramble_court.turn_in_text:
The Bramble Court is over. The approach is open.

You've done more for the Barrens than a battalion, and a battalion would have been given a banner for it.

Take these.

sb_the_pit_at_bael_modan.description:
Tarrik. Lie down before you come up to the rim - the glare's behind us and you'll be a shape on the skyline.

The dwarves at Bael Modan have been digging for years.

That's not news and it's not a war. People dig. I've watched this pit since before it had terraces and for most of that I wrote it up as mining and went home.

Here's what changed. I count heads.

Every month there are more miners, and every month the hole is deeper, and the two numbers are climbing together in a way that mining does not.

A mine slows down. You hit hard rock, you hit water, you hit the end of a seam, and the crew shrinks or moves. This one has never once slowed.

So I want fewer miners, and I want to know what they're digging toward.

They're not soldiers. They'll still swing a pick like they mean it.

And keep an eye on the bottom of that pit while you're down there. There's something in it.
sb_the_pit_at_bael_modan.accept_text: The terraces of the pit at Bael Modan.
sb_the_pit_at_bael_modan.turn_in_text:
And the pit's still going.

They didn't even stop to look at their own dead. That's the part that worries me, not the digging.

Take this.

sb_golem_cores.description:
The dwarves have built golems to haul rock.

Stone ones. Grey, square, and they thump up and down those terraces all day and all night, and they obey orders and they never tire.

That last part is what I'd like explained.

I've watched one of those things work a full cycle of the sun and then keep working, and nothing on this plain does that. A kodo stops. A dwarf stops - badly, and late, but he stops.

So something is running them and it isn't food and it isn't water.

I want to know how. I'd settle for a piece of one, which is all I've any right to ask for.

Crack one open. There's a core in the chest and it glows.

Bring me shards of it.

And don't spend too long thinking about what they're running on. I did that for a week and it got me nothing but a short temper.
sb_golem_cores.accept_text: Off the stone golems on the pit terraces. The core's in the chest.
sb_golem_cores.turn_in_text:
Interesting.

They're running on nothing. Or on something that is doing a very good impression of nothing.

I'll send word north. Take this.

sb_the_overseers.description:
Behind every dwarf with a pick there's a dwarf with a whip, and behind him there's one with a wrench.

That's the chain. Miners dig, overseers keep the miners moving, engineers keep the overseers supplied with everything that makes moving possible.

I've spent a month watching it work and I'll say this for it - it's a good chain. Nobody idles. Nobody waits for anything. Whatever else the dwarves are, they are not wasteful with a day.

And a chain breaks in the middle.

Not at the bottom. We've thinned the miners and they replaced them inside a fortnight and didn't lose an hour.

Take out the middle and the top has nobody to give orders to and the bottom has nobody giving them.

Overseers wear red sashes. Engineers carry wrenches the size of your arm.

Both. And in no particular order, as long as it's both.
sb_the_overseers.accept_text: On the pit terraces. Red sashes and the big wrenches.
sb_the_overseers.turn_in_text:
The pit's gone quiet. Whole terraces standing idle.

Nice work. There's one more thing to chase down there.

Take this first.

sb_grubbs_ledger.description:
Foreman Grubb Deepdelver has run this pit since before the Keep was built.

And he keeps a ledger.

Ore. Workers. Accidents - and I want you to notice that he counts the accidents, because a man who doesn't care is a man who doesn't write them down.

He counts everything. I've watched him stop a line, at cost, to get a figure right.

That's the whole reason I want those pages. A man who counts that carefully is a man who knows exactly what he's counting toward, and the number is in there somewhere even if the reason isn't.

Pages off the overseers' satchels - they carry the day's sheets up to him.

And Grubb himself, if he comes up for air.

He's stubborn. He's also paid by the cubic yard, which is the single most useful thing I've learned about him and tells you how he'll fight.
sb_grubbs_ledger.accept_text: Pages off the overseers' satchels, and Grubb himself in the pit.
sb_grubbs_ledger.turn_in_text:
Look at these numbers.

They've been digging for something specific. I don't know what it is.

They know where it is. That's worse.

Take your reward. I'll write this up tonight.

sb_eyes_on_the_gate.description:
Zhuul. Get down in the grass - no, all the way down, you're a shape from the wall at this distance.

I've been lying in this grass east of the Keep for two months with a spyglass and a bad attitude, and I'd like it noted that one of those is professional.

The dwarves have turned Bael'dun into a proper fortress. Riflemen up on the walls, patrols working the yard on a rotation I could set a clock by.

That's not a mining camp protecting itself. That's a garrison.

I need the gate scouted and the riflemen thinned before one of them spots me, which is a matter of time rather than luck at this point.

Walk up to the gate. Look. Come back.

If a rifleman objects, shoot him first.

I'd go myself. I'd leave a trail through this grass you could follow from the wall.

Trolls are tall, mon. It's the one part of the job I can't train out.
sb_eyes_on_the_gate.accept_text: The gate of Bael'dun Keep, east side.
sb_eyes_on_the_gate.turn_in_text:
Good. Good.

Gate's guarded - but not as well as they think it is, and that gap is the whole of my job.

Take this.

sb_mastiffs_at_the_gate.description:
The dwarves keep mastiffs. Big, loud, mean and loyal, and I've no complaint about any of those on their own.

They've started ranging out past the walls.

One of them found my last lean-to. Not the dog's fault and not mine - it was a good lean-to and it had held for six weeks.

But it means the perimeter they're watching is bigger than the one I planned around, and a spy who's planned around the wrong perimeter is a spy with a short future.

So I'd like the dogs gone. And while we're at it, I'd like what they've been guarding.

The sergeants walk them, and the sergeants carry dispatches. That's a dwarf's idea of security - put the orders next to the teeth.

A hound is not a good postman.

Bring me the dispatches. I don't read dwarvish.

I know a man who does and he owes me considerably more than this.
sb_mastiffs_at_the_gate.accept_text: Outside the Keep walls - the mastiffs and the sergeants walking them.
sb_mastiffs_at_the_gate.turn_in_text:
Four dispatches. Orders for the east gate.

The dwarves are digging in, which is a different thing from digging.

Take this.

sb_cut_the_fuse.description:
Now the one that's actually urgent, and I've been sitting on it for three days trying to be sure.

Bael'dun's explosives experts have run a charge-line to the east gate.

I've followed it with the glass as far as the rock. It goes up the cliff.

If that line is fired, it brings the cliff down on the Waystation road - and the Waystation road is how everything north of here gets anywhere, including the people who'd come and ask the dwarves about it afterward.

I don't think it's a threat. That's the part that's kept me up. I think it's a precaution, laid by somebody careful, for a day they expect.

I want the experts gone and the charges in my hands before that day turns up.

And yes - I know exactly what I'll do with them.

The experts wear the little red hats. Take their charges.

And don't drop them. I'm aware that sounds obvious. It is not obvious, if you've ever met a dwarf.
sb_cut_the_fuse.accept_text: Along the charge-line to the Keep's east gate. Red hats.
sb_cut_the_fuse.turn_in_text:
Five charges, all intact.

I'm impressed. Don't tell anyone I said so, I've a reputation that took years.

Take this.

sb_ironvein.description:
Sergeant Ironvein runs the Keep's east wall, and I've come to think he IS the east wall.

He drills the riflemen. He walks the mastiffs himself - the sergeants do it on paper, he does it in fact, at least twice a week.

And he hammers every plan flat before it leaves the yard. I've watched three officers walk out of that gate with an idea and come back without it.

That's a rare animal. Most garrisons rot from the inside because nobody's willing to say no to a bad plan.

If Ironvein falls, the east gate falls.

I've been wrong before and I'll own it. I was wrong about the mastiffs' range and it cost me a lean-to.

I am very sure about this one.

The sergeants are up on the walls. He's among them - listen for the hammer.

And dwarves fight better in lines than they do loose. So break the line first and take them one at a time after.
sb_ironvein.accept_text: On the Keep's east wall, among the sergeants. Listen for the hammer.
sb_ironvein.turn_in_text:
Ironvein down. The east gate's lost its anchor.

This is going to hurt them for a season, and they won't work out why for most of it.

Take this. You've earned it.

sb_windspire_harpies.description:
Alamir. Don't stand under the spires while we talk - I'll explain in a moment and you'll be glad I did.

The spires in the north-east are full of wind and voices, and I've stopped being able to tell you which is which.

Harpies nest in the hollows up there. They shriek down at anything that passes underneath, and it is not a warning and it is not territorial - I've watched them do it to an empty road.

I've hunted them a season.

My arrows are running low. My patience went some while before that, and I'd rather be honest about the order.

Feathers, claws, and a great deal of noise, out of the hollows on the east side.

And don't stand under the spires.

They drop things. Not on purpose, I don't think. It doesn't improve the outcome.
sb_windspire_harpies.accept_text: The hollows on the east side of the spires. Don't stand underneath.
sb_windspire_harpies.turn_in_text:
Quiet at last. You could almost hear yourself think up there.

Take this.

sb_voices_in_the_spires.description:
The wind sings through those spires. It has done since long before the harpies came and it'll do it after - that's the rock, not them.

The windcallers sing with it.

And where they sing, the dust gets up and turns on you. Not blows. Turns - I've watched a dust devil change direction against the wind to reach a traveller, which is the single most unnatural thing I have seen in this country.

So I want the windcallers silenced, and I want the crystals they carry.

The crystals sing too. They'll do it in a pocket, quietly, and they'll do it whether or not a harpy is holding them.

I'd rather they did it for me than for the harpies. That's the whole of my reasoning and I'm aware it's thin.

They're about the size of your thumb.

Take the crystals, break the devils, and come back before you start humming along. Everyone does. It takes about an hour.
sb_voices_in_the_spires.accept_text: Off the harpy windcallers in the spires. The dust devils follow the singing.
sb_voices_in_the_spires.turn_in_text:
They're singing in my pocket.

It's... not unpleasant.

Take this, and stop humming.

sb_skyshriek.description:
At the heart of the spires there's a hollow where the wind never stops.

Not slows. Stops - I've been to the lip of it at dead calm, on a day when nothing else out here was moving, and the air in that hollow was still going round.

A matron has taken it, and she's named herself after it.

She commands the windcallers and she sets the dust devils loose, and now I've seen where she does it from I understand why she can - she isn't calling the wind, she's sitting in the only place out here that already has some.

I want her gone before the next storm.

Because a storm plus that hollow plus a harpy who's worked out what to do with both is a thing I'd rather not find out the shape of.

The hollow's at the arch, near the east edge. Look for the biggest nest.

She'll scream. Ignore it - that's not the attack, that's the part before it.
sb_skyshriek.accept_text: The hollow at the arch, near the east edge of the spires.
sb_skyshriek.turn_in_text:
The wind's dropped. Listen to that.

Quietest the spires have been in years.

Take this.

sb_the_raptor_cull.description:
South of the spires is the Raptor Grounds. A long valley between two ridges, and the Sunscale nest the whole length of it.

I'm a hunter. So I'll tell you what this is before I ask, because I've had people take it the wrong way and go in there like it was a war.

It's a cull.

The grounds are overfull this season. Too many stalkers on the ridges, too many lashtails down in the valley, and nowhere near enough prey to carry them through to spring.

Left alone they'll eat the valley hollow and then starve in it, and the grounds don't come back from that inside a generation.

So: stalkers on the ridges, lashtails in the valley.

And leave the eggs.

I mean that as an instruction and not a kindness. I won't have it said I broke the balance - I'm correcting one.
sb_the_raptor_cull.accept_text: The Raptor Grounds south of the spires. Leave the eggs.
sb_the_raptor_cull.turn_in_text:
Good. The valley can breathe.

Take this.

sb_razorbeak.description:
Now something that isn't a cull, and I want the difference on the record after what I just asked you.

There's an alpha out there called Razorbeak and she has been raiding other nests.

Not for food. For the eggs.

She breaks them. One by one, and she doesn't eat them, and she doesn't take them anywhere - I followed her for two days to be certain, because I did not believe what I'd seen the first time.

The grounds are going quiet for it. Not thinner. Quiet, which is different and worse, because it means nothing is hatching.

I hate waste.

I hate it considerably more when it's deliberate, and I've had a week to decide whether an animal can be deliberate, and I've decided this one is.

The nest-mothers are protecting what's left of the clutches. They'll come at you first and they're right to.

Then her. She's fast - don't stand still.
sb_razorbeak.accept_text: In the Raptor Grounds, among the nests. Nest-mothers first.
sb_razorbeak.turn_in_text:
Razorbeak's gone. The nests will recover.

Take this, with my thanks.

sb_something_below.description:
You! Yes - mind the rope, that's load-bearing and so am I.

Fizzwick Boltcog. I found this crater last spring and I have been digging in it since, which my former partner describes as an obsession and I describe as a schedule.

I found a stair at the bottom. A STAIR. Cut, dressed, going down.

I found a great deal of glittering rock, which I will not be discussing.

And three days ago I found what I have written up in my own notes as 'a series of unfortunate bites'.

Sinkhole burrowers. They came up through the floor of my own dig, which is the one direction I had not budgeted for.

They are still coming.

Little brown things, lots of legs, extremely rude.

Thin them and I'll get back to work.

And no, you can't see what I've found. Nothing personal. You just can't.
sb_something_below.accept_text: Down in the crater dig. They come up through the floor.
sb_something_below.turn_in_text:
Marvellous!

I've sorted three crates already. Don't look at them.

Take this.

sb_tunnel_guards.description:
Below the burrowers there's a second thing, and it is not a bigger version of the first thing.

Tunnel-guards. Harder, bigger, and - this is what's actually stopping me - a great deal better organised.

The burrowers came up at random. These hold positions. They hold the SAME positions, every day, and they rotate off them, and I have sat and timed it with a glass because I am not going to walk into something I haven't timed.

They're keeping me off the stair.

I do not enjoy being kept away from things. It is possibly my defining characteristic and it has cost me two partners and a thumb.

So: the guards dead, and some of their chitin plates for my shop.

They ring when you tap them.

Don't tap them. Whatever answers that, you don't want to meet, and I know because I tapped one.
sb_tunnel_guards.accept_text: Below the burrowers, holding the way to the stair.
sb_tunnel_guards.turn_in_text:
Five plates! They'll fetch a fortune in Ratchet.

Don't tell my partner. Don't tell my former partner either, he'll want half out of spite.

Take this.

sb_vexa.description:
Bottom of the crater. Past the guards, past everything.

There's a queen down there and her name is Vexa, and the Sinkhole is hers - not occupied by her, HERS, in the way a house is somebody's.

The Broodspiral below is her nursery.

Now. I want the stair. That's been my entire object since last spring and I'm not going to pretend it's changed.

But I'd also like the nursery intact, and I'd like that said out loud by somebody who stands to profit from the opposite - because a thing like that going down takes the ring with it and nothing grows back in a crater.

I can't have either while she's alive. I've turned it over and there's no arrangement to be made with her.

Go down. Find the nest at the centre.

She's big, she's angry, and she will not stop.

Neither should you. That's not encouragement, it's the actual tactic.
sb_vexa.accept_text: The nest at the centre of the crater, below the guards.
sb_vexa.turn_in_text:
The queen is dead. The stair's open.

I'm going to need a bigger shovel.

Take this, with my deepest thanks and a cheque I will never in my life cash.

sb_down_the_stair.description:
Right. The stair.

It doesn't go down. That's the thing I need you to have in your head before you're standing on it.

It goes AROUND. It's a spiral, and I have measured it twice and gotten two different answers, which I find personally insulting - I measure well, it's the one thing nobody has ever disputed about me.

Drones and skulkers patrol the outer ring.

Thin them so I can get in there with chalk, because an unchalked spiral is how a person ends up walking the same ring for six hours convinced he's descending.

I had a customer once, few years back - fellow who turned up in Ratchet with no papers and a lot of questions about how the roads work here. He said where he was from, a man could be handed a map of anywhere on request.

Imagine that. A map, free, of somewhere you hadn't been. He said it like it was nothing.

Take the stair at the crater's edge and keep to the right-hand wall.

Stay with it and it'll bring you to the middle whether you like it or not.
sb_down_the_stair.accept_text: The stair at the crater's edge. Keep to the right-hand wall.
sb_down_the_stair.turn_in_text:
And you came back with all your fingers.

I'm adding that to the map. It's a data point.

Take this.

sb_amber_for_the_taking.description:
Now the part of this dig that pays for the rest of the dig.

The hive builds in amber.

And amber - I'll keep this brief, I'm told I don't - is worth more by the ounce than every single thing I have pulled out of this crater to date, combined, including the stair, which cannot be sold.

The weavers spin it. The spitters spit it. The best shards sit in the gland before either happens, which is why you want them off the creature and not off a wall.

I'd go myself. I have gone myself. That's how I know about the gland and it is also how I know about the spitters.

Don't drop them.

A shard that's cracked isn't worth a tenth, and they crack on gravel, and this entire crater is gravel.

I have thought about that problem for a month and the solution is apparently 'be careful'.
sb_amber_for_the_taking.accept_text: Off the hive weavers and resin spitters in the rings.
sb_amber_for_the_taking.turn_in_text:
Perfect clarity. And the one in the middle appears to be waving.

Take this, I need to sit down.

sb_the_tenders.description:
Past the outer ring the tunnel widens into a brood chamber.

The things that tend it are called brood tenders, and I've been told they are quite gentle.

I want to be scrupulous about my sourcing here, because it matters.

I was told that by somebody who is not coming back.

So I'm passing it on to you with the provenance attached rather than letting it sit in your head as a fact, which is more than anyone did for me when I started this dig.

The Broodkeeper sits at the head of that chamber. Behind a pair of resin pillars - you'll see them from the entry, they're the only straight lines down there.

Tenders first, then it.

And stay out of the green.

The green is not for you. I've no better way to put it and I've tried several.
sb_the_tenders.accept_text: The brood chamber past the outer ring. Stay out of the green.
sb_the_tenders.turn_in_text:
The Broodkeeper's dead and the second ring's open.

I'm very proud of you and also deeply afraid, and I'd like both noted.

Take this.

sb_screen_the_queen.description:
One more ring before the Queen's Hollow, and this one has a name that tells you what it's for.

The Larval Screen.

Crushers, larvae, and a great pale guard that watches the throne from the dark - and the word screen is the hive's, not mine. That ring isn't defending anything. It's hiding what's behind it.

If my maps are right, the Queen sits on the other side.

I'd rather you cleared the screen than found out how right my maps are, and I want you to notice the care in that sentence, because I've been wrong about this crater twice and both times somebody else paid.

Crushers first. Then the Broodguard.

It doesn't move much. It hits like a falling roof, which is the usual arrangement with things that don't move much.

The Queen's behind it.

Not today, though. Today you clear the screen and you come back out.
sb_screen_the_queen.accept_text: The Larval Screen, the last ring before the Hollow.
sb_screen_the_queen.turn_in_text:
The screen is down and you're alive.

I'll chalk the throne room in on my next trip, which I am already dreading and already planning.

Take this, with my gratitude and my apologies in advance.

sb_into_the_kraul.description:
Every thorn on that ridge grows out of the same root. I've said that for four winters and been laughed at for most of them.

The root is the Kraul.

The quilboar hill-warren south of my post, with a mouth of bramble and a throat of boars, and everything you've cleared off that ridge - the skinners, the hounds, Garn, Durga's hedge - came out of it.

I've watched that hill four winters.

It has never looked as busy as it does now, and busy is the only word I've got. More traffic at the gate, more smoke off the top, more of everything going in than coming out.

Something in there is being got ready.

The gate is south of my post, under the thorns. Spearhides at the door, beast trainers just inside.

Thin the gate guard before anything else.

Be quick, and keep your back to the wall. The wall is mostly thorn, which I'd call a joke if it weren't the actual advice.
sb_into_the_kraul.accept_text: The Kraul gate, south of the thornwatch post, under the thorns.
sb_into_the_kraul.turn_in_text:
Spears, whips, and all your fingers. You'll do.

Take this. We're going deeper.

sb_seed_and_thorn.description:
The thorns on that ridge aren't wild.

I need you to take that seriously, because everyone I report to treats it as a figure of speech and it is a flat statement of fact.

The geomancers inside the Kraul seed them. One barbed pod at a time, pushed into the ground by hand, and I have watched it done through a glass from the second bend.

Every pod is a little more hill the quilboar own.

That's how a thornwatch loses a ridge - not in a battle. A pod a day for ten years, and then one morning you notice your post is a hundred paces inside somebody else's country.

I want pods for my notes, because a drawing is an opinion and a pod on a table is evidence.

And I want the geomancers who make them put in the ground.

They carry them while they work, and they're almost always down on their knees doing it.

Handle the pods by the stem. They open if you squeeze them, and they do not close again.
sb_seed_and_thorn.accept_text: Off the Razorfen geomancers working the ground inside the Kraul.
sb_seed_and_thorn.turn_in_text:
The thorn's spreading faster than I'd feared.

And now I can prove it to somebody who outranks me, which is the whole point.

Take this.

sb_the_vine_bridge.description:
West of the first fork there's a rope-and-vine bridge over a drop, and on the platform at the far end lives Roogug.

He's been ordering that hill's warriors about since before I was a ranger.

And here's the argument I keep having with my own officers: he's off the main road.

Which makes him safe to leave alone. That's true, strictly. Nothing he does threatens the ridge directly and no patrol of mine has to pass him.

I'd rather he were not left alone.

Because a quilboar who has been giving orders for thirty years and never once been tested is a quilboar everybody in there still listens to, and that's worth more to the Kraul than the ground he's standing on.

The bridge is narrow. Don't fight on it - that's how you lose a party one at a time.

Wait for them on the platform. Roogug will come to you.

He's all muscle and no plan. Use that.
sb_the_vine_bridge.accept_text: The vine bridge west of the first fork, and the platform beyond it.
sb_the_vine_bridge.turn_in_text:
Roogug's down. The bridge is quiet for the first time in my life.

Take this, with my thanks.

sb_two_speakers.description:
North of the fork the Kraul splits around the Thorn Court, and a chieftain sits at either end of it.

Aggem Thorncurse, west. He calls the boar-spirits.

Death Speaker Jargba, east. He speaks for the dead and - this is the part that matters - he takes what they tell him extremely seriously.

I've spent four winters working out which of them actually runs this hill and the answer is neither, and that's why both have to go.

They keep the heartbeat. Between the two of them the whole warren knows what it's doing on any given day, and stopping either makes it stumble.

Whichever order you like. I've no preference and I'd be inventing one.

Aggem's guards are beast-trainers with boars. Jargba's are Death's Head, with hexes.

Don't fight both courts at once. The Thorn Court is open ground and it'll pull them together if you stand in the middle of it.

And don't let either one finish a sentence.
sb_two_speakers.accept_text: The Thorn Court, north of the fork - Aggem west, Jargba east.
sb_two_speakers.turn_in_text:
Both of them!

I'd call the hill's spirit broken, but I've been out there long enough to know better.

Take this, and my respect.

sb_the_pens_below.description:
At the centre of the Kraul are the Boar Pens.

A corral ring with stalls on every side, and in the middle of it Overlord Ramtusk, who has been fattening boars for a war for a decade.

Ten years. I want that number to land, because I've had it a while and it still does.

That's not a raiding herd. You don't need ten years for raids - you need a season and a bad winter. Ten years is somebody who has a date in mind and has had it since before I took the post.

I want the pens broken before anybody opens them.

Sows in the stalls, the Overlord in the ring.

The ring has three gaps. Hold the south one and they'll come to you through it - that's the only way this fight is manageable, because the open version is a hundred boars and no corners.

And keep the sows off your back. They'll come round while you're looking at him.
sb_the_pens_below.accept_text: The Boar Pens at the centre of the Kraul. Hold the south gap.
sb_the_pens_below.turn_in_text:
The Overlord's down and the pens are empty.

I'll sleep tonight. Four winters, and I'll sleep tonight.

Take this. You've earned it.

sb_the_beast_pit.description:
From the pens a narrow neck runs north-west, and it's sealed.

Not barred. Warded - stones set into the rock, held by Ward-Keepers who do nothing else, in a hill where everybody does three jobs.

That's the Beast Pit.

There's a thing in it called Agathelos, and they've been feeding it on stolen kodo for years. Our kodo, off that ridge, which is where a great many of Taurajo's missing animals went and nobody ever found a track.

The ward-stones keep it in.

So understand what I'm asking: break four and the ward falls, and then it is not in anymore.

I've thought hard about leaving it sealed. The seal is holding. But it's holding because quilboar maintain it, and the day they decide to open that neck themselves is a day they choose and not one we do.

Ward-Keepers hold the neck. Break the stones, then go in.

Agathelos is a beast, not a boar. Don't mistake one for the other. It isn't kind about that.
sb_the_beast_pit.accept_text: The warded neck north-west of the pens. Break the stones, then go in.
sb_the_beast_pit.turn_in_text:
Agathelos is dead and the pit's open to the sun.

I hope that rattles Charlga. I think it will.

Take this.

sb_razorflank.description:
Top of the Kraul. A platform of bones, a hut of thorn and tusk, and Charlga Razorflank sitting in it.

She's heard the pens fall. She's heard the speakers die. Nothing you've done in that hill has been a secret from her and I'd rather you went in knowing that than thinking you had surprise.

The hill's heart is hers. That's not a flourish - the thorn on that ridge grows because she wants it to, and I've got four winters of measurements that say so.

Take it, and the thorns wither by spring.

I've wanted to say that sentence to somebody capable of doing it since my first winter out there, and I've rehearsed it, and it's come out smaller than I expected.

Totemics around her. She mends them as fast as you cut them, so cutting them is a losing proposition and always has been.

Go for her first if you can.

The thorns won't forgive you for it. They'll stop, though.
sb_razorflank.accept_text: The bone platform at the top of the Kraul.
sb_razorflank.turn_in_text:
Charlga's dead.

The Kraul will take a generation to recover, if it recovers at all, and that ridge will breathe for the first time since anybody in Taurajo was born.

Take this, with all the thanks a ranger has in her.

sb_blind_hunter.description:
There's a hunter in the western galleries and I'd have called him a story six months ago.

He's been blind for years. Everyone in that hill knows it. And he does not miss.

I've lost two scouts to him - good ones, both of them quiet, and quiet is exactly the wrong qualification against a man who's listening.

The second one was carrying nothing. No pack, no mail, soft boots, and he was taken clean through the dark at a range my best archer couldn't make with his eyes open.

So he isn't guessing. Something about that gallery carries sound to him and he has spent years learning the shape of it.

The handlers guide him. Take them - that's not a kindness to him, it's that a blind hunter who's being walked to you is a different problem from one who has to find you.

West gallery, past Aggem's pen.

He listens for you. Don't stand still.

And don't breathe loudly either, if it comes to that. I'm aware of how that sounds.
sb_blind_hunter.accept_text: The west gallery of the Kraul, past Aggem's pen.
sb_blind_hunter.turn_in_text:
The hunter's down, and I'll write to the families properly now.

Take this, and my thanks.
